title: Top Koszul Ext on a constant-rank open
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], let $\mathcal I$ be its kernel ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $C=i^*\mathcal I$ be its tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Use the derived category and derived internal Hom of [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and write $F^q=H^q(R\mathcal Hom_Y(i_*\mathcal O_Z,\mathcal O_Y))$. Let $V\subseteq Z$ be open and $n\in\mathbb N$. Assume only for $z\in V$ that an affine neighbourhood of $i(z)$ cuts out $i$ by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence] and that $\operatorname{finrank}_{\mathcal O_{Z,z}}C_z=n$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. Set $N=\mathcal Hom(C,\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Then $(i^*F^n)|_V\cong\bigwedge^n(N|_V)$, for the exterior sheaf [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. No hypotheses are imposed away from V; the assertion is about top cohomology only.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ, lemma-regular-immersion-ext, Koszul cohomology calculation and local comparison

proof.text: At every z in V choose an affine Koszul chart of length m. Choose the conormal basis and use the affine conormal frame to compute its stalk finrank as m. The given constant finrank hypothesis implies m=n.

Construct the actual scalar-to-self Ext coefficient map induced by the pullback-pushforward adjunction unit O_Y -> i_*O_Z. Apply derived internal Hom, degree-n homology, tensor pullback, then restriction to V. The length-n local coefficient lemma makes every stalk map bijective. Reflect the isomorphism using the stalk criterion for module sheaves.

The all-degree self-coefficient Ext comparison on the regular locus identifies the codomain with the nth exterior sheaf of the restricted conormal dual. Compose this comparison with asIso of the coefficient morphism.

based_on.place: Lemma 48.15.5, canonical coefficient map to self Ext and Lemma 48.15.4

proof_origin.note: Compiling reduction to local coefficient bijectivity and the all-degree self-Ext exterior comparison; the rank identification and stalk detection are proved from existing declarations.
